deep.reconstruction: Context: in his 1983–84 notes on systems of pseudo-lines (pseudo-droites), Grothendieck builds a space 𝒳 by gluing local pieces. Each piece is a polygonal cell Δ_D attached to a pseudo-line or stratum D. Its boundary ∂Δ_D carries arcs that encode the specialization and generalization operations between neighbouring configurations D and D'. The aim is that 𝒳 come with a natural map 𝒳 → X, presumably to the ambient 'space of pseudo-lines' or projective/dual model; X is not identified on this page. The gluing has two independent choices. (i) The transition isomorphism ω_D → ω_D' between orientation data is either parallel transport or its opposite. (ii) A specialization arc b on ∂Δ_D is glued either to the arc obtained from b by parallel transport or to the antipodal arc. The previous page records that his earlier attempt had both choices wrong, and announces a list of the four possibilities. This page treats family A, the gluings that 'donnent lieu à une application naturelle 𝒳 → X'. There the identification α is obtained by parallel transport composed with the antipodal map, and correspondingly the orientation transition ω_D → ω_D' is opposite to parallel transport (always β = b). Case A1 (α = a'): b on ∂Δ_D is glued to the generalization arc a' on ∂Δ_D' antipodal to b, i.e. opposite to the parallel-transported one. Then 𝒳 → X is an immersion (locally injective), compatible with the polygonal structure. His intuitive reading: a generalization of D' is marked by the arc toward which the 'blue stroke' moves D'; that stroke 'pulls' (tire) D' toward itself. Case A2 (α = a): b is glued to its parallel transport. Then 𝒳 → X is an immersion on each face F* but folds (rabattement) along the common boundary of two adjacent faces. Here the blue stroke 'pushes' (pousse) D' to generalize it. The next page treats family B, where the transition is parallel transport. There he discards both cases as giving intuitively absurd circuits: they move away from D instead of turning around it. Overall, the page is a careful sign and convention analysis whose goal is a consistent gluing making 𝒳 a locally faithful (immersed) model over X. A1 appears to be the convention that works.
errors: No mathematical error can be confirmed; the page is itself correcting earlier sign/convention errors (described on the previous page).

There is a possible internal tension: the opening of A says the identification is by transport composed with the antipodal map, whereas A2 glues b to its plain parallel transport. A2 is presumably listed as the 'wrong-arc' variant within family A, which is consistent with the four-way case split.
Neither X nor the immersion claims are proved here; they are asserted from pictures.

ideas.what: Four-way case analysis of gluing conventions (orientation transition = ±parallel transport; arc identification = parallel transport or antipodal), with a test for whether the resulting map 𝒳 → X is an immersion or has folds
ideas.modern_name: sign/orientation conventions in constructing a cell complex (or branched/étale cover) of pseudoline configurations; local injectivity versus folding of a cellular map
ideas.usually_credited_to: general cellular topology; pseudoline arrangement spaces: Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Folkman–Lawrence (1978)

ideas.what: Heuristic 'pull versus push' interpretation of generalization arcs: the blue stroke 'tire' (pulls) versus 'pousse' (pushes) D'
ideas.modern_name: orientation of mutation/flip moves in pseudoline arrangements

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a canonical gluing of local polygonal cells of pseudo-line data into a space 𝒳 with a natural immersion to X. He identifies one convention (A1) as giving an immersion and another (A2) as giving a fold along common edges. A completed construction of such a 'space of pseudo-lines' as an immersed or étale cellular model does not appear on this page and is not known in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: Alors 𝒳 → X est une immersion ... Maintenant 𝒳 → X est une immersion sur chaque face F*, mais c'est un [rabattement] le long d'une [frontière] commune : deux faces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could bear on combinatorial models of the space of pseudoline arrangements (the topology of Ringel/Goodman–Pollack spaces, or realization spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids). However, the page is too fragmentary to extract a definite result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page fixing orientation and gluing conventions in an unpublished construction. The fold-versus-immersion dichotomy is a nice detail, but it is routine convention-checking with no standalone result.
